title: Epidermolysis bullosa (EB)
summary: Inherited skin fragility in which minimal friction causes blisters. Recognise it, handle the baby gently, and refer urgently to a specialist EB centre. Primary care supports under the specialist plan.

hero.alt: AI diagram showing the level of split in EB types

glance.think: A neonate or infant with blisters and erosions from minimal friction (hands, feet, nappy area), ± absent skin at birth, nail dystrophy or mouth blisters.
glance.engine: Inherited defects in adhesion proteins; the level of split defines the type (simplex, junctional, dystrophic, Kindler).
glance.backbone: Urgent referral to an EB centre, gentle handling, no adhesives, and soft silicone dressings under specialist guidance.
glance.never_miss: Airway involvement (hoarse cry in JEB), sepsis, dehydration or failure to thrive, and SCC in chronic RDEB wounds.

what: A group of **inherited mechanobullous disorders**: skin (and often mucosa) blisters after **minimal trauma**, because adhesion molecules are defective. This is different from **EB acquisita**, which is autoimmune and usually affects adults.

figure.caption: Skin fragility in EB: the level of the split in EB simplex, junctional and dystrophic EB compared with normal skin.

cause: Loss of structural integrity at a specific skin level means minor shear causes a blister. Inheritance is autosomal dominant or recessive depending on subtype. **Key Module 6 links: DEB is caused by type VII collagen (COL7A1) defects, and chronic RDEB wounds carry a high risk of cutaneous SCC.**

list: Blisters and erosions at **friction sites** (hands, feet, belt line, nappy area). They may be present at birth.
Nail dystrophy, milia and scarring (especially dystrophic types). Mitten deformities in severe RDEB.
**Mucosa:** mouth, oesophagus (dysphagia), larynx (hoarse cry in severe JEB).
Localised EBS often presents when the child starts **crawling or walking**.
A neonate with unexplained blistering, with or without congenital absence of skin: **consider EB until proven otherwise**.

diagnosis: Urgent recognition and referral to a **specialist EB centre** (UK: e.g. GOSH and other DEBRA-linked centres). Subtyping uses immunofluorescence mapping, electron microscopy and genetic testing. Primary care does **not** attempt to subtype.

head: Look-alike
Clues
rows: Localised; well baby; no family history

management.title: A specialist multidisciplinary disease
management.text: The IP and pharmacist role is recognition, safe interim handling, timely referral, and medicines support under the EB team’s plan.

list: **Refer urgently** any baby with unexplained fragility or blistering to paediatric dermatology or the EB team. For GOSH, contact the dermatology registrar via switchboard.
**Handle gently:** no adhesive tapes, lift on a soft pad rather than under the arms, keep the environment cool, and reduce friction.
Do **not** lance blisters unless trained in EB technique. Specialist nurses teach sterile piercing and silicone dressings.
**Dressings:** soft silicone or low-adherent, with no ordinary adhesives. Emollients and paraffin to lubricate.
Pain, constipation, nutrition, dental and eye care through the MDT.
Infection: colonisation is common. Discuss significant infection with the EB team.
**Medicines optimisation:** liquid formulations if there are oesophageal strictures, avoid rectal routes where possible, and check interactions.
Awareness: **Oleogel-S10** (birch triterpenes) is a specialist wound therapy for selected JEB and DEB wounds.
**RDEB:** surveillance for **SCC**. Any changing chronic wound needs urgent dermatology review.

red_flags: Respiratory distress or hoarseness (airway involvement in JEB).
Dehydration, failure to thrive, or sepsis.
A new, enlarging or ulcerating chronic wound in RDEB (**SCC**).
pearls: Give parents **DEBRA UK** support details early.
Genetic counselling for future pregnancies is a specialist role.
Never blame ‘rough handling’ alone when true fragility is present.
Even mild localised EBS benefits from a correct diagnosis (footwear and blister care education).
